This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded at the London City Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 1 Aug '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from Wunderground, specifically the highest temperature recorded for all times on this day for the London City Airport Station, available here: https://www.wunderground.com/history/daily/gb/london/EGLC.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the gear icon next to the search bar and switch the Temperature setting between °F and °C.

This market can not resolve until the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description:
**Latest official forecasts position 26°C as the clear market favorite.** The UK Met Office’s current guidance for London on August 1 projects a daytime maximum of 26°C under predominantly sunny skies with light northerly winds, aligning directly with the 62.5% implied probability. Updated model runs have moderated earlier July projections of 30–31°C, reflecting a weaker high-pressure ridge and slightly cooler maritime influence that has kept peak temperatures in the mid-20s range.

Supporting context includes typical early-August climatology (long-term average high near 22–23°C) and the urban heat-island effect, which can add 1–2°C in central London relative to rural stations. Hourly guidance shows temperatures climbing from morning lows around 16–17°C to afternoon peaks near 26–28°C before easing, with minimal cloud cover and negligible precipitation risk limiting further warming. Traders appear to be weighting the consensus official forecast and recent model consensus over longer-range seasonal signals of above-average warmth, resulting in tight clustering around the 25–27°C outcomes.

eventMetadata.context_description:
**High pressure building across southern England is positioning London for above-average warmth on August 2, with official Met Office guidance highlighting sunny conditions and maximum temperatures likely reaching 27–28°C.** 

This aligns with the market’s leading outcomes at 27°C (43.5%) and 26°C/28°C (combined ~45.5%), reflecting tight clustering around model consensus for a warm but not extreme day. Long-range outlooks from late July noted near- or above-normal temperatures, warmest in the south, with potential for hot spells under higher-than-average pressure—conditions that favor clear skies, light winds, and enhanced solar heating plus the urban heat island effect in central London. Recent model runs continue to support this without indicating rapid changes or significant cooling fronts. 

Traders are pricing in modest uncertainty from exact station readings (e.g., Heathrow vs. urban sites), possible localized cloud, or minor forecast revisions in the final 24–48 hours, keeping probabilities spread across the 26–28°C band while heavily discounting extremes below 25°C or above 29°C.

Historical analogs for early August under similar synoptic patterns rarely exceed 36°C without clear skies, supporting the low implied probabilities for 37°C or higher. Updated guidance ahead of the peak heating window will likely refine these probabilities as convective timing becomes clearer.

eventMetadata.context_description: **Market-implied odds favor a Tokyo daily maximum of 27–28°C on August 3, 2026.** Forecasters attribute this positioning to lingering cloud cover and scattered showers expected to limit daytime heating under a strengthening Pacific High, despite the broader seasonal outlook for above-normal temperatures across Japan. Historical climatology places average August maxima around 31°C, so traders are weighting short-term mesoscale influences—such as potential sea-breeze effects and modest model spread in the 48-hour window—more heavily than the long-range warmth signal. Updated JMA and global ensemble guidance expected in the next 24–48 hours will likely refine these probabilities ahead of market resolution.

eventMetadata.context_description: Traders assign the highest implied probabilities to a peak temperature of 28–30 °C in Munich on August 1 because current ensemble forecasts from the German Weather Service (DWD) and ECMWF models converge on a daytime maximum near 30 °C under weak high-pressure influence and light southerly flow. These conditions favor strong daytime heating from solar insolation while limiting cloud cover and mixing, consistent with the observed late-July warming trend across southern Bavaria. Urban heat-island effects in the city center and downslope warming from the Alps add a modest positive bias to official station readings. Recent model runs show little spread around this narrow range, keeping 31 °C or higher outcomes below 2 % combined probability and colder 27 °C or below scenarios at roughly 9 %. With resolution occurring at the close of the calendar day, any last-hour convective development or wind shift could nudge the final observed maximum, but the current atmospheric setup strongly supports the market’s clustering around 29 °C.

eventMetadata.context_description: **Market-implied odds favor a Tokyo daily maximum of 27–28°C on August 3, 2026.** Forecasters attribute this positioning to lingering cloud cover and scattered showers expected to limit daytime heating under a strengthening Pacific High, despite the broader seasonal outlook for above-normal temperatures across Japan. Historical climatology places average August maxima around 31°C, so traders are weighting short-term mesoscale influences—such as potential sea-breeze effects and modest model spread in the 48-hour window—more heavily than the long-range warmth signal. Updated JMA and global ensemble guidance expected in the next 24–48 hours will likely refine these probabilities ahead of market resolution.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded at the Tokyo Haneda Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 3 Aug '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from Wunderground, specifically the highest temperature recorded for all times on this day for the Tokyo Haneda Airport Station, available here: https://www.wunderground.com/history/daily/jp/tokyo/RJTT.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the gear icon next to the search bar and switch the Temperature setting between °F and °C.

This market can not resolve until the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent short-term forecasts from sources like timeanddate.com project a high near 27°C (81°F) for Tokyo on August 3, driven by overcast skies and passing showers that limit solar heating and enhance evaporative cooling. This aligns with the market's leading outcomes clustering at 26–28°C, reflecting trader consensus on reduced insolation amid typical early-August humidity and weak steering patterns. Broader seasonal context shows Tokyo averages near 31°C, but model runs highlight day-to-day variability from transient cloud cover rather than persistent high-pressure dominance. Upcoming Japan Meteorological Agency updates and refined model ensembles in the next 24–48 hours will likely refine these implied probabilities.
